questions.q: What are the two inputs to the basic cost-per-token formula?
options: The model's parameter count and its license type
GPU cost per hour and sustained tokens-per-second throughput
The number of developers on the team and their salaries
The programming language the serving framework is written in
questions.explain: Cost per token is GPU dollars per hour divided by sustained tokens-per-second throughput (converted to tokens per hour) — the two numbers the formula actually needs.

questions.q: Why does low GPU utilization dramatically increase the effective cost per token?
options: Low utilization makes the GPU physically consume more electricity
A GPU's hourly cost is fixed regardless of how busy it is, so the same bill is spread across far fewer tokens when utilization is low
Low utilization causes the GPU to process tokens faster
Utilization has no effect on cost per token
questions.explain: You pay for GPU time whether it's busy or idle. At 20% utilization, the same hourly cost is spread across roughly a fifth of the tokens it could otherwise produce, multiplying the effective cost per token.

questions.q: Why do commercial LLM APIs typically price output tokens higher than input tokens?
options: It's an arbitrary business decision with no technical basis
Output tokens are generated sequentially (decode), which is more compute-expensive per token than the parallel prefill pass used for input tokens
Input tokens are actually more expensive, but providers round down
Output tokens require no GPU compute at all
questions.explain: Prefill processes the whole prompt in one parallel pass (cheap per token), while decode generates tokens one at a time sequentially (expensive per token) — pricing reflects that real compute asymmetry.

questions.q: In the example cost calculation, what does the function cost_per_million_tokens compute?
options: The total number of GPUs a company owns
GPU dollar cost per hour divided by tokens produced per hour, scaled up to a cost per million tokens
The exact market price every vendor charges for a token
The number of requests a model can serve per day
questions.explain: The function converts tokens/sec to tokens/hour, divides the hourly GPU cost by that to get cost per token, then multiplies by one million to report cost per million tokens.

questions.q: What determines whether self-hosting a model is cheaper than a pay-per-token API?
options: Self-hosting is always cheaper regardless of usage
How consistently high the utilization of the self-hosted GPU can be kept — low, spiky utilization often favors pay-per-token, while high, sustained utilization often favors self-hosting
Pay-per-token APIs are always cheaper regardless of usage
The choice has no effect on overall cost
questions.explain: Self-hosting pays for fixed GPU-hours regardless of load, so it wins at high, consistent utilization; a pay-per-token API shifts utilization risk to the provider, which often wins at low or spiky usage.
